note: Field-standard terms that the claim-support checks read as claims. Every entry below was written against a named false positive in the 74-document benchmark; the `evidence` field quotes the sentence that produced it. An entry must be narrow enough that the same word still fires when it really is a claim — 'improved water source' is excused, 'improved survival' is not.

entries.reason: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme service-level labels. 'Improved', 'unimproved' and 'safe' are the published category names for water and sanitation facilities, not assertions that anything was improved or is safe.
evidence: Improved water sources included piped water in the household, public tab, borehole, protected dug well, protected spring, rainwater collection and bottled water.
Water hygiene and sanitation (WASH) facilities present in the household were categorised into improved and unimproved.
Unsafe drinking water defined as no access to piped water, public taps, stand-pipes, tube wells, boreholes, protected dug wells and springs and rainwater.

entries.reason: Text quoted from a reporting guideline checklist (PRISMA, STROBE, CONSORT, TRIPOD, MOOSE). The wording belongs to the guideline, and 'results in a synthesis' is a noun phrase rather than the verb 'results in'.
evidence: Reporting bias assessment | 14 | Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).
Discussion | 23a | Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence.

entries.reason: A conditional clinical instruction. 'If improved' and 'if not improved' state the observation that selects the next step in a treatment algorithm; they assert no causal effect.
evidence: Repeat bolus in second hour if improved.
If shock not improved after 1 hour of IV fluid, give whole blood at 10 mL/kg slowly over at least 3 hours

entries.reason: The sentence reports a measured quantity rather than attributing an effect. The observational branch of the causal check fires without consulting the evidence in the sentence, so a described magnitude is excused here instead.
evidence: In severely malnourished children VH is consistently reduced: in Gabon4, mean VH was 218μm (SD 43) and CD was 154 (17) μm in 13 children with SAM.

entries.reason: Standard associational phrasing in epidemiology. 'At increased risk of' describes a rate difference between groups and is the conventional way to avoid claiming an effect.
evidence: There is evidence from a number of setting that children with disabilities are at increased risk of SAM and evidence from high income settings shows that early multidisciplinary interventions can improve functional outcomes.
